recs.stt: It's Way Too Easy to Get a .gov Domain Name
recs.x:
An alarming amount of societal functionality depends on what effectively amounts to the honor system. This is especially true when it comes to any sort of gatekept specialty profession, like coroners for example.

There was a great talk at DefCon about faking death: [link]

recs.stt: What to do if the bank says you're dead
recs.x: On the subject of people being declared dead, there's a good defcon talk about abusing how easy it is to declare someone dead. "Chris Rock - I Will Kill You" [link]

cites.x: Reminds me of a DefCon speaker that talked about exploiting a bunch of websites to order death and birth certificates. Really eye opening, and potentially devastating if it's done to you. Edit: [link]

cites.stt: Three Years in Identity Theft Hell
cites.x: This is mainly an issue of authentification and as long as your credentials remain crappy/easy to guess/easy to forge (like the US SSN system), that long it will stay easy to game the system.

cites.stt: Facebook ordered to explain deleted profile
cites.x: It's not only Facebook who have this process unsufficiently secured. The process for administering real death is also not really tamperproof.
